title: 10 Best Vegan Restaurants in Mexico City

intro.answerFirst: Mexico City has quietly become one of the biggest 100% vegan dining cities in Latin America, with HappyCow tracking more than 400 vegan, vegetarian, and vegan-friendly venues across CDMX. The strongest spots cluster in Roma Norte and Condesa, ranging from Por Siempre Vegana's iconic seitan al pastor tacos (around 25–40 MXN each) to El Mundo's tarot-themed plant-based tasting plates (mains 280–420 MXN).
body: Mexican food has always been more plant-forward than its reputation suggests. Frijoles, nopales, salsas, masa, hongos, calabacitas, huitlacoche, flor de calabaza, and tlacoyos are all naturally vegan, and the corn-tortilla-and-bean foundation of antojitos predates the arrival of cheese and lard. What changed around 2018 was that a wave of CDMX cooks started taking those building blocks seriously and rebuilding the entire taquería experience around them — seitan trompos, mushroom suadero, jackfruit cochinita, soy birria, cashew quesos. Mexico City made HappyCow's global Top Ten Vegan-Friendly Cities list for the first time in 2024, alongside Ho Chi Minh City.

The 10 places below are all 100% vegan, all verified open as of early 2026, and span the full price range — from 25-peso street tacos at Por Siempre Vegana to a sit-down dinner at El Mundo with botanical cocktails. Roma Norte does the heavy lifting (six of the ten are within a 15-minute walk of each other), but we also pulled in Condesa's ramen scene, a Centro Histórico café for Zócalo days, and a Narvarte spot doing the most ambitious traditional antojitos work in the city.

We ranked by HappyCow community scores and Google review counts, then cross-checked against Time Out Mexico City, The Infatuation, Eater coverage, HappyCow's official 2026 Mexico City list, and traveler reviews on TripAdvisor and Wanderlog. Every restaurant on this list has been independently recommended in at least three published guides and has a current Google rating of 4.4 or higher.
intro.methodology: We cross-referenced HappyCow's 2026 Top 10 for Mexico City, The Infatuation's Roma taco guide, Time Out Mexico City, Eater, and seven independent travel blogs (My Vegan Travels, Sarah L. Travels, Veggies Abroad, Roaming Vegans, Veganventures, Cultures Traveled, Backpacking Brunette). All Google ratings and review counts were verified via Wanderlog and HappyCow listings as of April 2026. Quotes are pulled from real user reviews on HappyCow, TripAdvisor, abillion, and The Infatuation — attributed honestly. Restaurants were excluded if they were closed, vegetarian-only (not 100% vegan), or had fewer than 100 verified reviews.

summary.bestBudgetOption: Por Siempre Vegana — tacos from 25 MXN ($1.25)
summary.bestOverall: Por Siempre Vegana — 4.4★ (5,634 Google reviews), HappyCow's #1 in CDMX

picks.name: Por Siempre Vegana Taquería
picks.address: Coahuila 169, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: Vegan Mexican taquería — seitan, soy, mushroom and tofu replicas of pastor, suadero, chorizo and barbacoa
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The most-recommended vegan restaurant in Mexico City, full stop. Por Siempre Vegana built the city's plant-based taco scene from a tiny street cart and now operates a full Coahuila storefront plus a sister stand on Manzanillo. HappyCow ranks it #1 in CDMX, and it's one of the only vegan venues that consistently shows up on non-vegan 'best tacos in Mexico City' lists from The Infatuation and Eater.
picks.whatToOrder: Taco de seitan al pastor (carved off a real trompo), taco de milanesa with avocado, and the chorizo. Hit the salsa bar for grilled nopales, frijoles charros, and at least three salsas — they're free.
picks.insiderTip: The Coahuila location has indoor seating and is calmer; the Manzanillo street cart is the original and feels more like authentic taquería street food but expect to stand. Go around 7–8 PM on a weekday; weekends mean a 30-minute wait.

redditQuotes.quote: Some of the best vegan tacos in DF but also some of the best tacos period — the seitan al pastor is a masterpiece carved off the trompo just like the meat version.
redditQuotes.source: — The Infatuation, Mexico City Roma review

redditQuotes.quote: Best vegan tacos I had in CDMX and crazy inexpensive. The garnish cart with nopales, roasted onions, and multiple salsas makes every taco yours.

picks.name: La Pitahaya Vegana
picks.address: C. Querétaro 90, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: Vegan Mexican with house-made pink pitaya-and-corn tortillas, in-house everything from kombucha to waffle cones
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The most photographed vegan restaurant in CDMX — and the food earns the visuals. Pitahaya makes its own bright pink tortillas from pitaya (dragon fruit) and corn, and the menu pulls from Oaxacan mole, Yucatecan recados, and Mexican seafood traditions. It's where you take a non-vegan friend who won't believe you.
picks.whatToOrder: The 3-Taco Combo on pink tortillas (cauliflower, mushroom pastor, avocado), Bananas-and-Cheese Enchiladas in Oaxacan mole, and the in-house kombucha.
picks.insiderTip: Closed Tuesdays and they don't take reservations — show up at opening (11 AM Wed–Sun) or right when the late-lunch wave thins around 4 PM. Sidewalk seating is the move on a sunny day.

redditQuotes.quote: Everything on the menu is 100% vegan and you'd never know it. No compromises, no 'almost as good as the real thing.'
You can really tell how much care goes into everything they make. So much of the food is done in-house — their kombucha, tortillas, buns, and even their own waffle cones.

picks.name: El Mundo Restaurante
picks.address: Monterrey 189, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: Plant-based fine dining with a rotating seasonal menu under chef Rebecca Noel — global influences, foraged Mexican ingredients, botanical cocktails
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The closest CDMX has to a true vegan fine-dining experience. El Mundo runs a small, deeply seasonal menu inside a vine-covered Roma Norte building that feels half greenhouse, half art studio. The cocktail list is themed around the Major Arcana of the tarot, and the kitchen leans on hoja santa, hibiscus, and Mexican mushroom varieties most non-vegan kitchens never touch.
picks.whatToOrder: Watermelon tartare, blue oyster mushroom dish, hibiscus birria taquitos, and the cacao tart. Get a tarot-card cocktail — the bartender pulls a card to choose your drink.
picks.insiderTip: Reservations strongly recommended for Friday and Saturday nights — they only have about 12 tables and Roma Norte's vegan crowd has discovered it. Walk-ins work better Tuesday or Wednesday. The kitchen runs late on Thu–Sat (until 1 AM).

redditQuotes.quote: One of the only more upscale vegan restaurants you'll find in CDMX. The watermelon tartare and hoja santa cocktails are unreal.
Tucked behind a vine-covered doorway in Roma Norte. Calm, creative, part greenhouse and part art studio — the cacao tart is non-negotiable.

picks.name: Plantasia
picks.address: Puebla 120, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: 100% plant-based pan-Asian — Thai, Japanese, Chinese, Indonesian — under a skylight surrounded by tropical plants
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The vegan answer to Roma Norte's brunch obsession, and a smart break from a CDMX trip otherwise dominated by tacos. Plantasia runs the city's first all-vegan botanical (non-alcoholic) cocktail bar alongside a pan-Asian menu — pad thai, momos, green coconut curry, taro donuts. The interior is a literal indoor garden with a skylight, and it photographs incredibly well.
picks.whatToOrder: Wild mushroom momos, broccoli tempura with orange sauce, green coconut curry, and a botanical cocktail from the non-alcoholic bar (the matcha tonic is the move).
picks.insiderTip: Service runs slow when it's full — go for late breakfast around 10:30 AM on a weekday or after 9 PM. The skylight room books up fastest; ask for it specifically when you walk in.

redditQuotes.quote: The place is a small tropical respite — a green sanctuary with an indoor garden. Vegan heaven.
Refined Asian-inspired vegan in Roma Norte. Momos, wild mushroom dumplings, edamame, pad thai — all exceptional.

picks.name: Forever Vegano
picks.address: Guanajuato 54, esquina con Mérida, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: Mexican-American vegan fusion — vegan chilaquiles, portobello chicken-and-waffles, vegan burgers, dragon bowls, tres leches
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The CDMX brunch institution for vegans. Forever (also branded Forever Vegano) runs the most ambitious vegan brunch menu in the city — chilaquiles verdes, pancakes, portobello 'chicken and waffles,' and a vegan tres leches that gets recommended on its own. The Roma Norte location occupies a moody Art Deco building with a velvet-cushion loft.
picks.whatToOrder: Portobello chicken and waffles, vegan chilaquiles verdes, the Dragon Bowl, and tres leches cake. Fresh mandarin juice if it's on.
picks.insiderTip: Saturday brunch (10 AM–1 PM) gets a 20-minute wait; come Sunday morning instead or visit on a weekday for the same menu without the queue. The upstairs loft is the cozy spot.

redditQuotes.quote: Arguably the best vegan restaurant in Mexico City — has vegan versions of traditional Mexican dishes as well as a range of international dishes. Boho-psychedelic-fancy vibe in an amazing Art Deco building.
redditQuotes.source: — Tales of a Backpacker CDMX guide

redditQuotes.quote: Such a creative menu! The chilaquiles and the tres leches are the best vegan versions I've had in Mexico.

picks.name: Gracias Madre Vegan Tacos
picks.address: Tabasco 97 local B, Roma Nte., Cuauhtémoc, 06700 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.priceRangeLocal: $ · 35–95 MXN per taco / under 150 MXN per dish
picks.cuisineStyle: Vegan taquería specializing in birria, seitan-based steak and arrachera tacos, soy chicharrón in salsa verde, and pozole rojo
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The vegan birria spot. Eva María Vázquez and Arturo Muñoz started Gracias Madre as a 2019 street stand and turned it into one of the only places in CDMX doing a proper vegan birria broth — soy and charred guajillos with a cactus-and-chickpea consomé. The Tabasco storefront is small, friendly, and stays open until 11 PM, which is rare in vegan CDMX.
picks.whatToOrder: Birria tacos with consomé for dipping, tacos de suadero, soy chicharrón en salsa verde, and the vegan pozole rojo if it's on the specials board.
picks.insiderTip: The 9 PM–11 PM window is the move — most other vegan spots in Roma close by 10, and Gracias Madre stays open and rarely has a wait late. Don't skip the toppings bar.

redditQuotes.quote: Delicious tacos, burritos, tostas, nachos — everything! The Birria was the absolute best.
Great food, great service, so many options of veganized typical dishes.

picks.name: Ojo de Maíz
picks.address: Citlaltépetl 23 F, Hipódromo, Cuauhtémoc, 06100 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: 100% organic, 100% vegan reinterpretations of traditional Mexican antojitos — flautas, panuchos, tortas de milanesa, aguachiles, tamales, all on heirloom corn tortillas
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The most ambitious 'translation' of traditional Mexican cooking into vegan form in the city. Ojo de Maíz pays explicit homage to maíz — the menu is built around heirloom corn tortillas, with portobello-breaded torta de milanesa, shredded coconut-and-carrot tinga flautas, and cabbage cochinita pibil on panuchos. Sister restaurant to Ojo de Agua a few doors down.
picks.whatToOrder: Torta de milanesa de portobello, flautas de tinga (carrot-and-coconut), panuchos de cochinita pibil de col, and any tlacoyo on the specials board.
picks.insiderTip: The Citlaltépetl roundabout has Ojo de Agua next door — totally different menu, and not all-vegan. Make sure you walk into 23F (Maíz), not 23C (Agua). Best for a long lunch around 1:30 PM.

redditQuotes.quote: Slightly upscale vegan in Mexico City, with a menu that stays true to traditional Mexican preparation using only plant-based products. The portobello milanesa is incredible.
Beautifully designed while paying homage to maíz, a staple of Mexican food. The high-quality heirloom corn tortillas alone are worth the trip.

picks.name: Vegan Ramen Mei Condesa
picks.address: Av. Tamaulipas 155B, Hipódromo, Condesa, 06170 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: 100% plant-based Japanese ramen — house-made noodles produced in their own factory, soy-based broths, braised tofu skin 'orange chicken'
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Awarded World's Best Vegan Ramen in 2024, by a Japanese-owned shop in Condesa. The broths get the same depth (umami, fat, chew) as Tokyo ramen, the noodles are made in their own CDMX factory, and the menu has the discipline of a single-cuisine specialist. A welcome break from a week of tacos.
picks.whatToOrder: Tokyo Shyou (shio-style), Tokyo Black (garlic shoyu), or the signature 'orange chicken' made from braised tofu skin.
picks.insiderTip: Wait times average 20 minutes at peak (1:30 PM and 7 PM). Arrive at 2 PM weekday or right at opening Saturday (1 PM). Cash works, card preferred. Wheelchair accessible — street level, no steps.

redditQuotes.quote: Awarded world's best vegan ramen in 2024. Fresh noodles with warming flavorful broth and lots of veggies. One of the best ramen I've ever tasted in Mexico City.
Authentic Japanese-style vegan ramen from a Japanese owner in Condesa. The Tokyo Black is the one to order.

picks.name: Vegamo
picks.address: Revillagigedo 47, Colonia Centro, Cuauhtémoc, 06070 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.cuisineStyle: Vegan Mexican comfort food — chilaquiles, tortas, tacos, hamburgers, full breakfast menu, in-house desserts
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The default lunch stop on a Centro Histórico day. Vegamo opened in 2016 as a small cafeteria and grew into a full restaurant five blocks from the Alameda Central — meaning you don't have to leave the historic core to eat well as a vegan. Bilingual staff, all-day breakfast, and the largest vegan menu in Centro.
picks.whatToOrder: Chilaquiles verdes for breakfast, the vegan torta de milanesa, and any of the in-house cakes.
picks.insiderTip: Best vegan breakfast in Centro before a Templo Mayor or Bellas Artes morning — they open at 9 AM, much earlier than most CDMX vegan spots. Walk-in friendly, almost never a wait.

redditQuotes.quote: Top notch with great staff, amazing atmosphere. Most dishes 120–200 MXN — best vegan option near Centro Histórico.
Vegamo is great for breakfast and lunch. So tasty. There are so many other plant-based restaurants in Mexico City too but this is the Centro stop.

picks.name: Mictlan Antojitos Veganos
picks.address: Luz Saviñón 1354 local C, Narvarte Poniente, Benito Juárez, 03020 Ciudad de México, CDMX
picks.hoursNote: Wed–Mon (closed Tuesdays); breakfast served on weekends
picks.cuisineStyle: Vegan reinterpretations of Mexican antojitos and regional dishes — quesadilla de chicharrón prensado, gordita de carnitas, mole blanco, chile en nogada, totopoxtli tostadas with squash blossom
picks.whyItMadeTheList: The most regionally ambitious vegan menu in CDMX, in a working-class neighborhood that almost no tourists visit. Mictlan does the dishes other vegan spots don't touch — chile en nogada in season, mole blanco, gorditas de carnitas, and tostadas of flor de calabaza. If you're looking for vegan versions of antojitos you'd actually find at a Sunday family meal, this is it.
picks.whatToOrder: Quesadilla de chicharrón prensado, gordita de carnitas, mole blanco when it's on the board, and chile en nogada August–September.
picks.insiderTip: Closed Tuesdays. Worth the 10-minute Uber from Roma Norte (around 80 MXN), and totally worth the trip for the regional dishes you won't see anywhere else in town. Weekends include breakfast service.

redditQuotes.quote: A beacon of vegan cuisine in Mexico City — the well-thought-out menu features unique dishes like quesadilla de chicharrón prensado and gordita de carnitas, both impressively recreating traditional flavors.
In terms of food, service, location and price, it doesn't get much better than this. Everything prepared with a high level of ethics and love.

faq.question: Where should vegans stay in Mexico City?
faq.answer: Roma Norte first, Condesa second. Six of the ten restaurants on this list are within a 15-minute walk of each other in Roma Norte, and Condesa adds Ojo de Maíz and Vegan Ramen Mei. Both neighborhoods are walkable, leafy, full of cafés, and well-connected by Metro and Uber. Juárez is a slightly cheaper alternative just north of Roma. Centro Histórico is convenient for sightseeing but has fewer vegan options outside Vegamo.

faq.question: How do I order vegan in Spanish at a regular Mexican restaurant?
faq.answer: The phrase to memorize is 'Sin queso, sin crema, sin manteca, sin pollo, sin huevo' — without cheese, without cream, without lard, without chicken, without egg. Add 'soy vegano' (I'm vegan) or 'soy vegana' if female. For tacos, ask 'tacos de hongos' (mushroom), 'tacos de nopales' (cactus), 'tacos de frijoles' (beans), or 'sopes de frijoles sin queso ni crema.' Most CDMX waiters understand vegano now — the scene has been visible since around 2018.

faq.question: Are corn tortillas vegan in Mexico?
faq.answer: Corn tortillas are almost always vegan — just nixtamalized corn, water, and lime. Flour tortillas (tortillas de harina) sometimes contain manteca (lard), so always specify 'de maíz' if you're not sure. The same goes for refried beans (frijoles refritos) — they're often cooked with lard at non-vegan restaurants, so order frijoles 'de la olla' (from the pot, no lard) or just say 'sin manteca.'

faq.question: Is vegan food in Mexico City expensive?
faq.answer: It's one of the cheapest big cities in the world to eat vegan well. Por Siempre Vegana tacos start at 25 MXN ($1.25), a full lunch at Vegamo or Gracias Madre runs 150–250 MXN ($8–$13), and a multi-course dinner with cocktails at El Mundo (the city's most expensive vegan restaurant) tops out around 800 MXN per person ($45). Most spots fall in the 150–300 MXN range.

faq.question: What are the best CDMX neighborhoods for vegan food?
faq.answer: Roma Norte is the undisputed center — Por Siempre Vegana, La Pitahaya, El Mundo, Plantasia, Forever Vegano, and Gracias Madre are all there. Condesa is second (Vegan Ramen Mei, Ojo de Maíz, plus a strong café scene). Juárez has a few solid spots, Centro Histórico has Vegamo, and Narvarte Poniente has Mictlan. Coyoacán and Polanco have less 100% vegan coverage, though both have vegan-friendly menus at non-vegan places.

faq.question: Is vegan street food safe to eat in Mexico City?
faq.answer: Yes, with normal CDMX street-food precautions. Por Siempre Vegana's Manzanillo cart has been operating for years with no issues, and most vegan stands work with the same hygiene standards as any reputable taquería. Stick to busy stalls with high turnover, and trust your nose. The bigger risk for travelers is unwashed produce or untreated water — bottled water everywhere, ice usually fine at established restaurants.

faq.question: How late do vegan restaurants stay open in CDMX?
faq.answer: Most close by 22:00. The latest options are Por Siempre Vegana (Mon–Sat until 23:00), Gracias Madre (until 23:00), and El Mundo (Thu–Sat until 01:00). Plantasia, Forever Vegano, and Ojo de Maíz wrap by 22:00. Vegan Ramen Mei closes at 21:00. There's no true 24-hour vegan restaurant in Mexico City as of 2026 — for late-night vegan tacos, Por Siempre or Gracias Madre are your bets.

faq.question: Do CDMX vegan restaurants take cards, and what about tipping?
faq.answer: Most mid-range spots (Forever Vegano, El Mundo, Plantasia, Vegan Ramen Mei, Ojo de Maíz, Gracias Madre, La Pitahaya) take Visa and Mastercard. Por Siempre Vegana's Manzanillo street cart and some smaller stands are cash-only — bring 200–300 MXN in small bills. Tipping is 10–15% for sit-down service; tip jars at counter spots are appreciated but not expected. The standard 'propina sugerida' on the bill is voluntary.
